newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to allow warrant issues soon, official says.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to allow warrant issues soon, official says.

text.p: Taiwan's vice-finance minister said on Thursday his ministry would soon allow local and foreign institutions to issue warrants on Taiwan blue-chip stocks.
"We have resolved most technical problems, so we will allow warrants issuance as soon as possible," Wu Chia-sheng, vice-finance minister, told reporters.
Wu did not give an exact timetable.
Taiwan Stock Exchange Corp, the island's main stock exchange, said on Wednesday it has completed a proposal on warrants issuance, but said it would need final approval from the finance ministry.

Under the proposal, the exchange would allow local and foreign banks or securities brokerages to issue warrants on domestic blue chips having a market value of more than T$30 billion and 25 percent or more of their shares circulating in the market.
To be eligible, listed companies also must have more than 7,500 shareholders, officials have said.
More than 20 local listed firms, including Cathay Life, Chang Hwa Bank, First Bank, Hua Nan Bank, Nan Ya Plastics, Formosa Plastics and China Steel, qualify under the proposed guidelines.
